While there is no guaranteed method for 100% anonymity 100% of the time, there are several ways to improve your security and privacy at home and online. A great place to start is to improve your operating system security. The various Linux kernels are generally accepted as being more secure platforms than Windows. Open source systems are much more difficult to slip backdoors into because of the shear numbers of eyes reading through the code. Ubuntu has a simple, easy to use interface with tons of support for the absolute Linux beginner. Debian is a bit more technical and has several more advanced security builds. Check out Kali Linux for an advanced penetration testing distribution and Tails for a live system that you can start on almost any computer.

Encryption is your friend. Use full disk encryption and encrypt your web traffic. Most of today's BIOS will have an option for full disk encryption. LUKS is the standard for Linux hard disk encryption. There are a few ways to keep your web traffic anonymized that have become well known for their heightened levels of encryption. The Tor Browser Bundle being the most well known is simple to use and comes set up with add-ons to stay safer online. Another type of encryption for web traffic is I2P. It's a bit slower but growing. The last option I'll suggest for web traffic anonymization is a VPN. Most VPN's are paid services, however an open source is available for this as well, OpenVPN.

As far as actual email services are concerned, the provider doesn't really matter as long as you use end-to-end encryption. Use an email client like Thunderbird, similar to Outlook for Windows, with the Enigmail and TorBirdy extensions. Be sure to create an OpenPGP key associated with your email address using GnuPG.

Using these methods, you can obtain nearly any level of desired security and privacy.
